# czc-v2026.10.26.3 (0.2.18.2)

Makes GPT OAuth diagnostics and gateway requests use consistent Codex protocol
handling, while isolating users, threads, tool rounds and WebSocket sessions.
Tibo health probes remain enabled by default. This release does not claim that
a relay is indistinguishable from a native CLI or guarantee upstream account
classification.

## Changes since czc-v2026.10.26.2

- Tibo probes, account tests, Responses-based image tests, compaction tests,
  429 recovery probes and legacy quota probes share Codex HTTP request
  preparation, headers, metadata, zstd compression and TLS selection. Scheduled
  and intelligent tests inherit the same path. Tibo retains its HTTP health
  measurement, interval and verdict rules.
- Diagnostics retain their existing account-state and traffic-admission
  policies. A background health probe does not start recording business
  authentication failures or consuming the local business-request limiter.
  Shadow-account diagnostics use the credential owner's TLS profile. API-key
  and direct image endpoints retain their separate protocol contracts.
- Preserve parent/child thread, fork and turn relationships while isolating
  identities by credential owner and downstream key. Anonymous requests no
  longer share sessions solely because their prompts or cache keys match.
  Retries within the same request keep their identity.
- Messages bridging now keeps the account's client family and configured
  prompt-cache policy. Custom keys remain custom, omitted keys stay omitted,
  and session-derived keys follow their declared policy. Turn state is
  isolated by actual session and thread, not by a shared cache prefix.
- Ordinary HTTP and passthrough forwarding share optional header and metadata
  handling, including valid caller-supplied W3C traces. Native environment
  facts and tool schemas remain intact. The gateway no longer invents local
  tools, permissions or skills, or renames third-party tools without adapting
  their arguments and results.
- Managed OAuth HTTP-to-WebSocket sessions prewarm once with `generate=false`.
  Native WebSocket clients and API-key paths do not receive duplicate prewarm
  frames. WebSocket fallback is scoped to the logical client session instead
  of disabling every session on the same account.
- OAuth WebSocket passthrough uses the account-aware Codex transport. Failed
  upgrades read framed error responses and close their connections. Native
  turn state is carried in frame metadata rather than the upgrade headers.
- Delta histories exceeding 2048 items invalidate the old chain instead of
  truncating history while retaining a full-response anchor. Anonymous
  connections have local state and cannot preempt each other through a cache
  key. Scheduling affinity remains separate from conversation state.
- Freeze UA, originator, version and protocol profile for a logical session.
  Automatic version updates accept only verified releases, currently 0.163.0
  and 0.164.0; explicit administrator version overrides remain available.
- Add official Codex 0.164.0 fixtures for initial prewarm, tool continuation,
  HTTP fallback, HTTP and WebSocket authentication recovery, and V2 compaction.
  Replay captured HTTP requests through both gateway forwarding routes and
  validate both 0.163.0 and 0.164.0 TLS/header baselines.

## VERSION

`0.2.18.2`

## Upgrade guidance and compatibility

- No database migration, frontend source change or mandatory configuration
  change is included.
- `gateway.openai_tibo_route.enabled` remains `true` by default.
- `gateway.openai_ws.prewarm_generate_enabled` now defaults to `true` for
  managed OAuth HTTP-to-WebSocket sessions. An explicit `false` is retained.
  Existing explicit transport/fidelity settings are respected.
- Legacy account-wide WebSocket retry/capability TTL configuration keys remain
  readable, but no longer expire a logical session's HTTP fallback. Session
  registries are bounded to 8192 entries with a 24-hour idle lifetime; restart
  or eviction ends the local session and rebuilds state.
- Clients needing cross-request continuation should supply actual session
  and thread identity. A cache key alone is no longer treated as conversation
  identity. Native Codex clients already provide the appropriate metadata.
- Third-party clients must execute the tools they declare. Undeclared shell,
  edit and stdin tools are no longer inserted just to resemble a CLI. Explicit
  account environment configuration is still supported.
- Restarting the service closes existing streams and clears in-memory
  connections; clients should reconnect with complete usable context.

## Verification

Passed on the implementation/integration tree before packaging:

- Full backend unit suite: `go test -count=1 -tags=unit ./...`.
- Docker-backed integration run: all packages except one timing-sensitive
  service test passed initially. The complete service package then passed
  with `go test -count=1 -tags=integration ./internal/service`.
- The initially failing, unchanged
  `TestBillingOutboxWorker_RenewsFinalizationLeaseUntilBlockedFinalizeReturns`
  passed 20 consecutive isolated repetitions. Its 40 ms lease is sensitive to
  concurrent compiler/test load; no billing code or assertion was changed.
- Full backend `go vet -tags=unit ./...` and golangci-lint v2.14.0 with zero
  issues after the release lint cleanup.
- Focused Codex/session/diagnostic/transport tests after lint cleanup, plus
  race detection for session versions, anonymous requests, child-thread
  turn state, WebSocket fallback, delta state and passthrough isolation.
- Official 0.164.0 binary captured against isolated local fake upstreams;
  two independent captures compare equal after normalizing dynamic values.
  Test fixtures record binary/source checksums and contain synthetic tokens.
- Frontend ESLint, TypeScript checks and Vitest: 392 files, 2957 tests passed.
- `git diff --check` and Go formatting checks.

Failed, interrupted or not performed:

- Early release checks were interrupted and restarted; incomplete runs were
  not counted as successful.
- The first lint run reported unchecked returns/type assertions and unused
  functions introduced by the refactor. These were fixed and lint rerun.
- One concurrent Go compiler was killed by the system and one command timed
  out. The affected checks passed with bounded compiler concurrency/memory.
- The integration timing failure described above is retained here rather
  than hidden by the successful rerun.
- No real authenticated OpenAI production request or account-classification
  test was performed. Capture uses local fake upstreams, a rejecting proxy
  and a strace network guard; a separate network namespace was unavailable.
- Browser end-to-end tests and the backend e2e target were not run. The latter
  references a script absent from this checkout. Frontend tests emitted
  existing mock/i18n warnings without failing.

Packaging must rebuild the frontend immediately before the `-tags embed`
server build from this exact tag, with `main.ReleaseURL` set to this origin
release. Installation is accepted only after the root page returns HTTP 200,
the installed version is `0.2.18.2`, and the running update-check response
reports this same release URL.

## Rollback

Restore the binary backed up during this deploy as
`/opt/sub2api/sub2api.bak.czc-v2026.10.26.3-<UTC timestamp>` and restart
`sub2api.service`, or rebuild and deploy `czc-v2026.10.26.2` (`0.2.18.1`).
There is no database migration to undo. Verify HTTP 200, version `0.2.18.1`
and the previous origin release URL after rollback. In-memory sessions and
connections are recreated after either upgrade or rollback.
